stories.title: Liquid Bitcoin sidechain: 'white hats' return $270M, keep $47M, as network preps restart
stories.summary: Attackers took roughly $320 million in Bitcoin from the Liquid sidechain, forcing the network to pause. The group, described as "white hats," has since returned about $270 million and asked operators "is that ok?" after keeping around $47 million. Liquid is now preparing to restart the network.
stories.whyItMatters: A major sidechain pause and a multi-hundred-million-dollar fund movement raises real custody and security questions for anyone holding assets on Bitcoin layer-2 networks.
whatToWatch: Whether Liquid completes its restart and confirms network integrity
Whether the remaining funds are returned or kept as a self-declared bounty
Any official post-mortem from Liquid's operators
questions: Were the 'white hats' authorized, or is this a hacker negotiating a return under a friendlier label?
What vulnerability allowed the initial withdrawal?

sources.title: Liquid recovers 3,400 BTC as hacker asks “is that ok?” after pocketing $47 million in Bitcoin
Liquid ‘white hats’ return $270M in Bitcoin as network prepares restart

stories.title: Ethereum's 2029 quantum-resistance deadline starts to reshape protocol roadmaps
stories.summary: Developers are increasingly designing around Ethereum's 2029 target for quantum-resistant upgrades, according to CryptoSlate. Separately, a seven-year-old blockchain project says it will abandon its own network and move to Ethereum, and a new arbitrage study found block builders capture $5 in value for every $1 of ETH the network burns. Together the reports point to a network adjusting both its long-term security plans and its fee economics.
stories.whyItMatters: How Ethereum handles quantum risk and builder economics will shape validator incentives and which chains developers choose to build on for years to come.
whatToWatch: Concrete technical proposals tied to the 2029 quantum deadline
Details on the migrating blockchain's transition plan to Ethereum
Any protocol response to the builder-versus-burn findings
questions: What specific quantum-resistant cryptography will Ethereum adopt?
Does the $5-to-$1 builder advantage point to a fee-market problem that needs fixing?

sources.title: Ethereum’s 2029 quantum deadline is starting to reshape what gets built next
A seven-year-old blockchain is permanently abandoning its own network to seek refuge on Ethereum

stories.title: Uzbekistan launches pilot for government bond-backed stablecoin payments
stories.summary: Uzbekistan has begun a pilot program using a stablecoin backed by government bonds for payments, according to Cointelegraph. The move puts the country among a small group of sovereigns experimenting directly with bond-collateralized digital currency rather than only licensing private stablecoin issuers.
stories.whyItMatters: A state-run, bond-backed stablecoin pilot signals government appetite to control stablecoin infrastructure rather than leave it to private issuers.
whatToWatch: Scale and merchant or bank participation in the pilot
Whether other central Asian states follow with similar programs
questions: What entity manages the bond collateral and redemption guarantee?
Will the stablecoin be available to retail users or limited to government payments?

sources.title: Uzbekistan begins government bond-backed stablecoin payment pilot

stories.title: Robinhood's blockchain projected to generate $160M in annual fees by 2028: Bernstein
stories.summary: Bernstein analysts estimate Robinhood's own blockchain network could generate about $160 million in annual fees by 2028, according to Cointelegraph. The projection reflects growing Wall Street interest in brokerage-run chains as a revenue line, not just a trading feature.
stories.whyItMatters: A profitable in-house chain would give Robinhood a new revenue stream tied to crypto infrastructure, a model other brokerages may copy.
whatToWatch: Robinhood's actual chain usage and fee data as it scales
Competing brokerage or exchange chain launches
questions: How much of the projected fee revenue depends on speculative trading volume versus durable use cases?

sources.title: Robinhood chain to generate $160M in annual fees by 2028: Bernstein

stories.title: New Bitcoin whale cohort's unrealized gains hit $9B, raising sell-side risk
stories.summary: A newer group of large Bitcoin holders has built up roughly $9 billion in unrealized gains, according to Cointelegraph, a level analysts flag as a potential source of sell pressure if holders start locking in profits. The report frames this as a market-structure risk rather than a signal of an imminent selloff.
stories.whyItMatters: Large unrealized gains concentrated among recent whales can amplify volatility if these holders sell together, a dynamic worth tracking for near-term price risk.
whatToWatch: On-chain data for signs of whale distribution or profit-taking
Bitcoin price action around key gain-realization thresholds
questions: What price level would trigger meaningful selling from this cohort?

sources.title: New Bitcoin whales spark sell-side risk as unrealized gains hit $9B

stories.title: Hunter Biden launches 'LAPTOP' meme coin aimed at TRUMP token holders
stories.summary: Hunter Biden has launched a meme coin called LAPTOP that is explicitly marketed toward traders who hold or held the TRUMP token, according to Decrypt. The coin's positioning leans on Biden's public profile and appears aimed at drawing attention from the existing TRUMP-coin trading community.
stories.whyItMatters: A politically-charged meme coin targeting a rival's token base is a reminder that speculation, not utility, still drives large pockets of retail crypto trading.
whatToWatch: Trading volume and price action for LAPTOP in its first days
Any reaction from Trump-aligned crypto figures or the TRUMP token team
questions: Does LAPTOP have any stated utility beyond its meme and political branding?
Who controls the token supply and treasury?

sources.title: What Is LAPTOP? Hunter Biden's Meme Coin Targeting TRUMP Holders

stories.title: Swiss stablecoin sandbox moves into testing phase, adds two partners
stories.summary: Switzerland's stablecoin regulatory sandbox has entered its testing phase and added two new partners, according to Cointelegraph. The sandbox lets participants trial stablecoin-related products under regulatory supervision before a full launch.
stories.whyItMatters: Switzerland's supervised approach to stablecoin testing offers a template other regulators may watch as they decide how to oversee stablecoin issuance.
whatToWatch: Identities and roles of the new sandbox partners
Timeline for moving from testing to full regulatory approval
questions: What specific stablecoin products or use cases are being tested?

sources.title: Swiss stablecoin sandbox enters testing phase, adds two new partners

stories.title: Tether-backed crypto exchange freezes withdrawals after $7M leaves custody
stories.summary: A cryptocurrency exchange backed by Tether has frozen customer withdrawals after about $7 million left its custody, according to CryptoSlate. The cause, whether a hack, an internal issue, or something else, has not been established.
stories.whyItMatters: Any custody incident at a Tether-linked exchange draws scrutiny given Tether's central role in stablecoin liquidity across crypto markets.
whatToWatch: An official explanation from the exchange for the fund movement
When or whether withdrawals resume
Any statement from Tether regarding its involvement
questions: Was the $7 million lost to a hack, an error, or insider action?
How exposed are remaining customer funds?

sources.title: Tether-backed crypto exchange freezes withdrawals after $7 million leaves custody

stories.title: Circle to acquire Tazapay to expand USDC cross-border payments
stories.summary: Circle plans to acquire payments company Tazapay to expand cross-border use of its USDC stablecoin, according to Cointelegraph. The deal points to Circle building out payment-rail infrastructure directly rather than relying solely on partnerships.
stories.whyItMatters: Owning payment infrastructure would strengthen Circle's position against other stablecoin issuers and traditional cross-border payment providers.
whatToWatch: Deal terms and expected closing timeline
Integration of Tazapay's payment rails with USDC settlement
questions: How much of Tazapay's existing business will shift to USDC-denominated settlement?

sources.title: Circle to acquire Tazapay to expand USDC cross-border payments

stories.title: Polish court detains fifth suspect in Zondacrypto exchange investigation
stories.summary: A Polish court has ordered the detention of a fifth suspect in an ongoing investigation into the Zondacrypto exchange, according to Decrypt. Further details of the allegations were not disclosed.
stories.whyItMatters: A widening criminal investigation into a crypto exchange raises questions about the platform's conduct and the exposure of its remaining users' funds.
whatToWatch: Formal charges against the detained suspects
Any statement from Zondacrypto on its operating status
questions: What specific conduct is Zondacrypto or its staff accused of?
Are customer funds on the exchange affected?

sources.title: Polish Court Detains Fifth Suspect in Zondacrypto Exchange Probe

stories.title: Hunter Biden's new 'LAPTOP' meme coin courts traders who lost money on TRUMP
stories.summary: A new meme coin called LAPTOP, launched by Hunter Biden, specifically targets traders who lost money holding the TRUMP token, according to CryptoSlate. The launch leans on political notoriety rather than any disclosed product or utility.
stories.whyItMatters: The launch shows how meme-coin creators keep exploiting political rivalries and prior trading losses to attract speculative retail attention.
whatToWatch: Whether LAPTOP sustains trading interest beyond its launch news cycle
Regulatory or platform reaction to politically-themed meme coins
questions: What, if anything, backs LAPTOP's value beyond speculation?

stories.title: Ledger CTO warns AI bug hunters against 'attention farming,' urges responsible disclosure
stories.summary: Ledger's chief technology officer has called on AI-assisted security researchers to act responsibly and avoid what he called "attention farming" when reporting bugs, according to Cointelegraph. The comments point to a rise in AI-generated vulnerability reports, not all handled responsibly.
stories.whyItMatters: As AI tools lower the barrier to finding and publicizing security flaws, how researchers and vendors handle disclosure will affect trust in hardware wallets and other crypto infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Whether Ledger or other vendors publish formal guidelines for AI-assisted bug reports
Any specific incidents that prompted the comments
questions: What distinguishes legitimate AI-assisted research from 'attention farming' in practice?

sources.title: Ledger CTO urges AI bug hunter responsibility, warns against ‘attention farming’
